rationale.conceptual: The paper's method involves a custom Voronoi protocol (using RCP seeds for uniform grains), precise grain boundary identification (CNA), and a specific formulation of the Reuss mixture model. Translating this into correct code requires genuine understanding of the atomistic modeling, the algorithms for RCP generation, and the rationale behind the grain-size control, which is a multi-part, non-trivial method.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has many sequential stages: RCP packing via energy minimization, Voronoi tessellation with Voro++, construction of 3 atomistic configurations, LAMMPS MD relaxations and tensile tests for each, CNA post-processing, and least-squares fitting. Orchestrating LAMMPS, Voro++, Python analysis, and ensuring proper I/O across all steps makes this a long and fragility-prone execution that goes well beyond simple single-step tasks.

This demands deep understanding of the paper's method, molecular dynamics, and several interacting software components.
